items.rationale: The domestic swerve and impact are covered under §§2.6.1–2.6.3 and 4.5.2, and the battery health waiver disapplies the below-80% exclusion in §2.6.8. The supplier's uneconomic-repair report supports settlement under §7.1.10 at an estimated €850 gross for a new equivalent, less €50 estimated salvage; no scheduled deductible or sub-limit amount is supplied.
Section 7.1.9 limits payment to the pre-loss specification, already accounted for on line 1. The separately billed elective upgrade difference is excluded.

The tablet's impact-cracked screen is covered under §§2.6.2–2.6.4; it is assessed separately but shares the laptop's insured event. Allow €180 gross for a like-for-like screen and fitting under §§7.1.7 and 7.1.10, with no separate deductible.

Section 5.2.3 covers necessary diagnostics for both affected units, including the laptop found uneconomic to repair. Allow €35 per device, or €70 gross for the combined line, below the shared €250 event cap and assuming no diagnostic fee was credited.
Under §§4.2.6 and 7.1.5, a carry bag must itself be damaged by the event to qualify. Replacing the undamaged bag alongside the laptop does not make it payable.
Sections 3.5(f) and 7.1.8(e) exclude the cost of future-performance undertakings, even when bought with a covered replacement.
Sections 3.5(d) and 4.3(c) exclude data recovery unless separately agreed. The battery health waiver does not provide data cover, and no data-restoration extension is shown.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separately billed administration charges, including those levied by another provider. The fee also relates to excluded data recovery.
